text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA
- Serbian government and competent ministries to undertake necessary measures to stabilise prices of meat on the market, including intervention from Serbia's commodity reserves.
- January-July average net wages rose around 25 percent, inflation in the seven months 3.3 percent, standard of living recovering gradually, according to analysts.

- Results of first round of multi-lateral compensation to clear inter-company debts to be known on Monday. Around 100,000 of 300,000 account holders estimated to have reported their outstanding debts.
- Imported cigarettes and drinks without excise stamps will be confiscated and destroyed under new regulations effective from August 1.
- Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce calls on government to revise Law on Customs Tariffs and reduce duties on imports of certain semi-finished products and equipment.
- Volume of short-term securities issued on the financial market is approaching the current size of money supply, says Yugoslav Securities Commission.

- Serbian government commissions Deloitte & Touche and Economics Institute of Belgrade to prepare study on transformation of Serbia's power company Elektroprivreda Srbije (EPS). Foreign partners interested in cooperation and investment in EPS, said EPS Board of Directors President Dragan Kostic.
- The Yugoslav government decides to raise imports of petrol and diesel fuel by 285,000 tonnes due to breakdown in installation at Pancevo refinery.
- Feketic-Subotica (near Hungarian border) 71-kilometer section of semi-highway to be opened to traffic in November. Construction works worth 400 million dinars.
- Text of agreement on representation of political parties in state media during election campaign published. Media campaigns to begin September 5.
NASA BORBA
- European Union in declaration on political development of Yugoslavia calls on Belgrade to accept OSCE observers for forthcoming Serbian presidential and parliamentary elections.
- A Belgrade municipal court calls for investigation against Serbian Radical Party leader Vojislav Seselj and his bodyguard for beating up lawyer Nikola Barovic.
- Despite court decision, several hundred radicals prevent Croat Barbalic family from returning to their Zemun flat from which they were evicted.
- Delegation of London club of creditors continues talks in Belgrade on reprogramming and repayment of Yugoslavia's debt to commercial banks estimated at around $2.4 billion.
- Zastava arms factory workers of Kragujevac announce march to Belgrade, protests outside Serbian government building on August 7.
- Beogradska banka A.D. likely to take over JIK and Slavija banka, two large banks whose licenses were revoked by the central bank due to insolvency.
- Owners of 453 private petrol stations in Serbia request permission from Yugoslav government for imports of 70,000 tonnes of fuel to prevent monopoly.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA
- Representatives of parliamentary parties in Montenegro reach agreement on need for early parliamentary elections which should be held in the first half of 1998.

- "(Montenegrin President Momir) Bulatovic's interpretation that there is no alternative to Yugoslavia is nothing but another name for a spineless and inferior Montenegro in that Yugoslavia," said Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic, ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) of Montenegro Vice President and DPS candidate for president of Montenegro.

- Serious politicians and statesmen should not underestimate the message of "street democracy" but neither accept its dictate which is as "productive" as the dictate of a certain political elite, Pobjeda says in a commentary on the protests against the visit on Monday by a senior Socialist Party of Serbia delegation to the Montenegrin president.
- Montenegrin air carrier Montenegro-airlines to start regular flights to Belgrade from August 7. Planes will fly from Podgorica and Tivat to Belgrade and back. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
